subject: A 13-year-old just rewrote history at the Asian Games
preheader: Plus aerobic distance work in the pool and rotational core on land this Monday.
heroHeading: Good morning swimmers and happy Monday
heroTeaser: A 13-year-old named Yu Zidi just swam herself to second place on the all-time 200 IM list, and the sport is still catching its breath.
outroLine: That's the week in the water. Happy swimming,

workout.dateLabel: Mon, Sep 21 · distance freestyle in the pool, rotational core on land

swimSet.title: Today's Swim Set
swimSet.description: A 3,050-yard aerobic distance session focused on finding a sustainable pace through long freestyle repeats, then finishing each block with a small acceleration to practice surging when fatigued.

lift.title: Today's Lift
lift.description: A rotational power and anti-extension core session aimed at building the midline stability that drives cleaner freestyle and backstroke through the water.

newsItems.title: 13-year-old Yu Zidi is now second all-time in the 200 IM
newsItems.body: Yu Zidi of China, just 13 years old, swam a 2:06.10 in the women's 200 IM at the 2026 Asian Games to claim the World Junior Record, the Asian Record, the Asian Games Record, and the second-fastest performance in the history of the event. Let that sink in for a second.

newsItems.title: Kim Youngboem breaks the Asian Games 50 free record at 20
newsItems.body: Kim Youngboem of South Korea set a new Asian Games Record in the men's 50 freestyle, breaking the mark previously held by his countryman Ji Yuchan from the last edition of the Games.

newsItems.title: Qin vs. Ohashi: the 100 breast showdown is on
newsItems.body: Day two finals at the 2026 Asian Games set up a marquee men's 100m breaststroke clash between China's Qin Haiyang and Japan's rising sensation Shin Ohashi, two of the most compelling breaststrokers in the world right now.

newsItems.title: Backstroker Nora McCarthy is headed to Princeton
newsItems.body: Nora McCarthy of Seattle Metropolitan Aquatic Club has verbally committed to swim for Princeton starting in 2027-28, bringing Ivy 'A' final-worthy times in the 100 and 200 backstroke to the Tigers' class of 2031.

athlete.name: Qin Haiyang
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: 喂！三点多啦，做么鬼！, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Qin Haiyang, born on 17 May 1999, is a Chinese swimmer who specializes in the breaststroke and individual medley. He trains under coach Cui Dengrong and made his first major international appearance at the 2018 Asian Games, where he won gold in the 4x100 metre medley relay.

At the 2023 World Aquatics Championships, Qin became the first swimmer in history to win all three breaststroke events at a single edition and set the world record in the 200m breaststroke. He won five gold medals at the 2022 Asian Games, was named its MVP, and became the first Asian swimmer named Male Swimmer of the Year by World Aquatics.
